gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Woodgod has a vintage, commanding look, its lowercase climbing almost to the capitals, while Noto Sans Wancho sets down a hulking, chalky sans with a gap in each e. Woodgod belongs up high, at display size.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-onest: Approachable Onest brings short ascenders and big bowls, with line thickness that barely changes, under Woodgod's commanding display letters. And over a full page, Onest's plain sans manner would keep the eye moving without any snags.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-open-sans: Modern and smooth, Open Sans leaves its curves unclogged and its lowercase bulky, set under the tall, vintage-flavored letters of Woodgod. But the strongest thing here is the gap in sizes of attitude: a loud display voice over a sans that simply gets on with it.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-parkinsans: Woodgod opens the pair with commanding, vintage display letters, lowercase stretching close to the capitals, while Parkinsans draws everything in single-weight rounded rods. Woodgod makes the statement; Parkinsans stays crisp and legible when shrunk.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-pt-sans-caption: Professional PT Sans Caption leaves its bowls unclosed and inviting, with big-bodied lowercase, beneath Woodgod's vintage display voice. And Woodgod's tall lowercase announces each line before the plain sans quietly carries on below.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-puritan: Rounded, friendly, a bit stubborn: Puritan keeps its forms open to the side and its e and a counters oversized, under Woodgod's vintage display letters. And across a full page, that sans would feel inviting and easy to settle into.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-questrial: Professional Questrial cuts open c, e and s shapes in a flat, stencil-like single weight, under a tall band of letters with short stalks. And Woodgod, with lowercase nearly reaching its capitals, handles the commanding part while Questrial handles the steady sans-serif reading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-radio-canada-big: Woodgod sets a commanding, vintage tone with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Radio Canada Big follows in a monoline sans-serif whose terminals finish clear of the stem and whose x-height fills the line, so a long page would read smoothly.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-saira: Rounded and see-through, with a visible gap in each s, Saira stretches its letters high toward the top line. Saira as a sans-serif body would run a long page cleanly beneath Woodgod's commanding, vintage display letters.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-sarpanch: Loud up top, tidy below: Woodgod's vintage lowercase climbs nearly to its capitals. Sarpanch then adds an open-mouthed e and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, a plain sans that lets Woodgod do the shouting.
